children: By Ken Nakao / Yomiuri Shimbun Staff Writer

Japanese regional railway operator Kyushu Railway Co. (JR Kyushu) plans to expand into the financial sector, including banking services. The firm wants to develop a new revenue stream as a declining population weighs on its railway business.
JR Kyushu will partner with major internet securities firm SBI Holdings Inc. to launch services in fiscal 2027, which ends in March 2028, according to sources.

The railway will use infrastructure provided by SBI Holdings to holistically manage and operate multiple financial services, such as for banking and securities. It plans to launch its banking service first and then expand into securities and other offerings.

Based in the southwestern Kyushu region, JR Kyushu operates a wide range of businesses, including real estate, hotels and retail. Non-railway operations accounted for about 60% of its consolidated operating revenue of about 500.3 billion yen in fiscal 2025. The railway has introduced a reward points program called JR Kyupo, where points are earned by riding trains and shopping at station buildings. The company aims to expand the reward ecosystem by entering the financial sector.

Other JR companies have made similar moves. In 2024, East Japan Railway Co. began banking operations with the help of Rakuten Bank Ltd. In May this year, West Japan Railway Co. entered into a capital and business alliance with Resona Holdings Inc. — which is a parent company of Kansai Mirai Bank Ltd. — with plans to begin banking services in fiscal 2027.
